paragraphs.source_en: Since the New Year began, I have gained a certain measure of fame; even as a cat, I feel my whiskers somewhat raised with pride, and this is indeed a matter for congratulation.

units.source_en: Since the New Year began, I have gained a certain measure of fame; even as a cat, I feel my whiskers somewhat raised with pride, and this is indeed a matter for congratulation.

ja.t: ぜらるるのはありがたい。

units.source_zh: 新年以来，我多少有了点名气，作为一只猫儿也有一点扬眉吐气了，真是可喜可贺。

paragraphs.source_zh: 新年以来，我多少有了点名气，作为一只猫儿也有一点扬眉吐气了，真是可喜可贺。

paragraphs.source_en: Early on New Year's morning, my master received a colored picture postcard. It was a New Year's greeting sent by a close friend of his, a painter; it was drawn in colored crayon, red at the top, dark green at the bottom, and in the center squatted an animal. In his study, my master examined it sideways and upright, and said to himself, "The colors are rather good." Having already admired it once, he ought to have stopped there, yet he kept turning it this way and that and looking at it without end. At one moment he twisted his body around, at another he stretched his arm out long like an old man having his horoscope read, and then again he faced the window and brought the card right up to the tip of his nose, staring at it incessantly. I wished he would stop at once, for sitting on his knees while they rocked to and fro was positively dangerous. At last his movements quieted down, and then I heard him murmur, "What on earth is this supposed to be?" It appeared that my master admired the colors on the postcard, but could not make out what the animal in the picture was, and so had been racking his brains over it all this time. I thought to myself, "Can this postcard really be so hard to understand?" With perfect composure I half opened my sleepy eyes, settled myself, and took a look; unmistakably, it was a portrait of me! Though this painter may not have fancied himself an Andrea del Sarto as my master does, he was certainly worthy of the name of painter, for both form and color were quite properly rendered. Anyone who looked at it would see that it was a cat. Moreover, it was so splendidly drawn that anyone with the slightest eye for such things would know at once that this was no other cat, but myself. When I considered that my master could not distinguish even so plain a matter and had to labor over it in this way, I felt humans were somewhat pitiable. If it were possible, I should very much like to tell him that the picture was me. Even if he could not recognize it as me, at least I wanted him to know that it was a cat. But human beings, after all, are animals incapable of understanding the language of our feline race; since they have not been blessed with that gift from heaven, I regretfully left the matter alone.

paragraphs.source_zh: 元旦一清早，主人就收到一张彩色明信片。这是他的一位知交画家寄来的贺年片，是用彩色笔画的，上方涂着红色，下方涂着深绿色，正中蹲着一只动物。主人在书斋里，把它横着看竖着看瞧了一遍，自言自语地说道：“色彩很不错嘛。”本来已经欣赏了一番，本该作罢，可是他仍然横过来竖过去看个不停。一会儿扭转身子，一会儿像老头儿让人家看“三世相”似的把胳膊伸得老长，一会儿又对着窗子，把画片拿到鼻子尖前看个没完。我真希望他赶快停下来，否则我坐在他的膝头上晃来晃去实在危险。他的动作好不容易缓和下来，这时只听他小声地说了句：“这究竟画的是什么呀？”看来主人很欣赏画片上的色彩，但却弄不清画上的动物是个啥东西，所以费尽心思一直在琢磨哩。我心想：“这画片真是那么让人看不懂吗？”我大大方方地半睁着睡眼沉下心去一看，货真价实，画的就是我的肖像！虽然这位画家未必像主人那样以安德利亚·特尔·萨尔德自居，但的确不愧是位画家，形体和色彩都画得很地道。让谁来看也是只猫儿。而且画得很出色，只要是个稍具鉴识眼力的人，一眼就会认出这不是别处的猫，正是我辈啊。主人连这么一清二楚的事也分辨不出，竟要如此绞尽脑汁，想来人类也真有点可怜。如果可能，我真想告诉他那就是我呀。即使认不出是我，至少得让他知道那是只猫儿。但是人类毕竟是不懂我们猫族语言的动物，他们没有受过老天的这份恩宠，所以很遗憾只好不去管它了。

paragraphs.source_en: Here I must say a word to the reader: humans have the bad habit of forever saying "cat, cat" at the slightest occasion, and of judging us with an offhand tone of contempt; this is highly improper. The notion that cows and horses are born from the dregs of mankind, and that cats are then manufactured from the dung of cows and horses, may be common enough among teachers who never notice their own ignorance and go about with arrogant faces; but to others it is truly unseemly. Though we may be cats, we are not made so roughly and handily as all that. Perhaps to outside eyes all cats look like one and the same thing, equal and indistinguishable, as though no cat possessed any character of its own. In truth, once you enter the society of cats and take a look, you will find it quite complex. The human saying "ten people, ten faces" applies just as well to our feline society. In the look of the eyes, the shape of the nose, the color of the coat, and the manner of walking, each is different. From the spread of the whiskers and the way the ears stand, down to the degree at which the tail droops, no two cats are the same. Beauty and ugliness, personal likes and dislikes, refinement and lack of taste: in all these things the variations are countless, and one may rightly call them endlessly diverse. Yet despite such obvious distinctions, human eyes, it is said, are always directed upward and do nothing but gaze at the sky; consequently, they cannot possibly understand our characters, nor even distinguish the details of our faces, which is truly pitiable. There is an old saying, I hear, that like seeks like, and it is exactly so: the rice-cake maker knows rice cakes, the cat knows cats, and when it comes to cats, only cats can understand. No matter how much humans may progress, in this one respect they are no good at all. And to speak frankly, since they are not nearly as great as they believe themselves to be, it is all the more impossible for them. How much less, then, could my unsympathetic master understand us, when he does not even grasp that mutual understanding is the foundation of love. The man is just like a perversely tempered oyster, clinging all day to his study and never once putting his head out toward the outside world. Yet he wears an expression as though he alone possessed a considerable breadth of insight, which is rather ridiculous. In fact, it is nothing of the sort: my portrait was plainly before his eyes, yet he did not notice it in the least, and instead said, "Since this is the second year of the war with Russia, perhaps it is a polar bear," uttering such an incomprehensible remark without the slightest embarrassment; from this it is clear that he has no breadth of insight at all.

units.source_en: Here I must say a word to the reader: humans have the bad habit of forever saying "cat, cat" at the slightest occasion, and of judging us with an offhand tone of contempt; this is highly improper.

ja.t: があるのははなはだよくない。

units.source_zh: 这里，须向读者声明一句：人类有个坏习惯，动不动就“猫儿、猫儿”的不离口，若无其事地使用轻蔑的口吻来评价我们，这是极不妥当的。

units.source_en: The notion that cows and horses are born from the dregs of mankind, and that cats are then manufactured from the dung of cows and horses, may be common enough among teachers who never notice their own ignorance and go about with arrogant faces; but to others it is truly unseemly.

ja.t: でもあろうが、はたから

units.source_zh: 那种认为从人类的渣滓中产生牛马，又从牛马的粪便中制造出猫儿来的想法，对于从来不知道自己无知、一向趾高气扬的教师们来说，也许是常有的事，可是在别人看来，这委实不成体统。

units.source_en: In truth, once you enter the society of cats and take a look, you will find it quite complex.
units.source_zh: 其实，只要你进入猫的社会里看一看，就知道里面也是相当复杂的。

units.source_en: The human saying "ten people, ten faces" applies just as well to our feline society.
units.source_zh: 人类所说的那句话：“十人十面”，同样也适用于我们猫儿的社会。

units.source_en: In the look of the eyes, the shape of the nose, the color of the coat, and the manner of walking, each is different.
units.source_zh: 从眼神、鼻子的形状、毛色、步伐等方面来说，都各有不同。

units.source_en: From the spread of the whiskers and the way the ears stand, down to the degree at which the tail droops, no two cats are the same.
units.source_zh: 从胡须张弛的模样，耳朵竖立的情况，到尾巴下垂的程度，没有一只猫儿是相同的。

units.source_en: Beauty and ugliness, personal likes and dislikes, refinement and lack of taste: in all these things the variations are countless, and one may rightly call them endlessly diverse.
units.source_zh: 可以说模样儿的美丑、个人嗜好、懂不懂风流等等真是千差万别，数也数不清的。

units.source_en: Yet despite such obvious distinctions, human eyes, it is said, are always directed upward and do nothing but gaze at the sky; consequently, they cannot possibly understand our characters, nor even distinguish the details of our faces, which is truly pitiable.

ja.t: しているにもかかわらず、

units.source_zh: 尽管存在如此明显的差别，可是据说由于人的眼睛只能是向上看，只知道仰望天空，所以不要说了解性格，就连识别我们相貌这类事也都无法做到，真是可怜得很。

units.source_en: There is an old saying, I hear, that like seeks like, and it is exactly so: the rice-cake maker knows rice cakes, the cat knows cats, and when it comes to cats, only cats can understand.
units.source_zh: 据说有句老话叫做“同类相求”，的确是这样，卖瓜的只认识卖瓜人，猫儿只认识猫儿，猫儿的事只有我们猫儿才了解。

units.source_en: No matter how much humans may progress, in this one respect they are no good at all.

units.source_zh: 不管人类如何进步，唯独在这一点上，他们是不行的。

units.source_en: And to speak frankly, since they are not nearly as great as they believe themselves to be, it is all the more impossible for them.

ともないのだからなおさらむずかしい。

units.source_en: How much less, then, could my unsympathetic master understand us, when he does not even grasp that mutual understanding is the foundation of love.

ja.t: であるということすら

units.source_zh: 更何况我那缺乏同情心的主人，就连相互了解才是爱的基础也不懂得，就更无法了解我们了。

units.source_en: The man is just like a perversely tempered oyster, clinging all day to his study and never once putting his head out toward the outside world.

units.source_en: Yet he wears an expression as though he alone possessed a considerable breadth of insight, which is rather ridiculous.

units.source_en: In fact, it is nothing of the sort: my portrait was plainly before his eyes, yet he did not notice it in the least, and instead said, "Since this is the second year of the war with Russia, perhaps it is a polar bear," uttering such an incomprehensible remark without the slightest embarrassment; from this it is clear that he has no breadth of insight at all.

ja.t: れぬことをいってすましているのでもわかる。

units.source_zh: 其实并非如此，明明我的肖像摆在他的眼前，可他一点也没有觉察出来，却说什么“今年是和俄国开战的第二年，大概画的是北极熊吧”，竟然说出这等令人费解的话而毫不脸红，足见他并没有远见卓识。

paragraphs.source_zh: 这里，须向读者声明一句：人类有个坏习惯，动不动就“猫儿、猫儿”的不离口，若无其事地使用轻蔑的口吻来评价我们，这是极不妥当的。那种认为从人类的渣滓中产生牛马，又从牛马的粪便中制造出猫儿来的想法，对于从来不知道自己无知、一向趾高气扬的教师们来说，也许是常有的事，可是在别人看来，这委实不成体统。虽说我们是猫儿，也决不会那么三下五除二，随便就能制造出来。也许从外人的眼中看来，所有的猫都是千态一体，毫无差别，好像每一只猫儿都没有本身的特色似的。其实，只要你进入猫的社会里看一看，就知道里面也是相当复杂的。人类所说的那句话：“十人十面”，同样也适用于我们猫儿的社会。从眼神、鼻子的形状、毛色、步伐等方面来说，都各有不同。从胡须张弛的模样，耳朵竖立的情况，到尾巴下垂的程度，没有一只猫儿是相同的。可以说模样儿的美丑、个人嗜好、懂不懂风流等等真是千差万别，数也数不清的。尽管存在如此明显的差别，可是据说由于人的眼睛只能是向上看，只知道仰望天空，所以不要说了解性格，就连识别我们相貌这类事也都无法做到，真是可怜得很。据说有句老话叫做“同类相求”，的确是这样，卖瓜的只认识卖瓜人，猫儿只认识猫儿，猫儿的事只有我们猫儿才了解。不管人类如何进步，唯独在这一点上，他们是不行的。而且说句老实话，他们并不像他们自信的那样伟大，所以就更无法做到。更何况我那缺乏同情心的主人，就连相互了解才是爱的基础也不懂得，就更无法了解我们了。他这个人活像脾气乖僻的牡蛎，整天蜷伏在书斋里，从来没有向外界探过头。但他却摆出一副只有自己颇有远见卓识的面孔，真是滑稽可笑。其实并非如此，明明我的肖像摆在他的眼前，可他一点也没有觉察出来，却说什么“今年是和俄国开战的第二年，大概画的是北极熊吧”，竟然说出这等令人费解的话而毫不脸红，足见他并没有远见卓识。
